Formulation
- Predisposing factors:
  - Family history of migraine (mother and sister).
- Precipitating factors:
  - Recent onset over three days; possible work-related stress; possible dehydration suspected by patient.
- Perpetuating factors:
  - Inadequate analgesic response to current self-administered ibuprofen regimen; ongoing screen exposure at work; photophobia/visual disturbance impacting function.
- Protective factors:
  - Social supports (housemates, family), help-seeking behavior and engagement with clinician, employment (access to follow-up), willingness to implement self-management (headache diary, reduce screen brightness).

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Probable migraine / acute headache
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Obtain effective symptom relief and reduce pain to enable return to normal functioning at work.
  - Identify triggers and prevent recurrence if possible.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide effective acute analgesia and symptomatic management.
  - Monitor for resolution or progression; identify need for prophylactic therapy if recurrent.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Follow clinician guidance on analgesia (use medications as advised).
  - Keep a headache diary to document frequency, triggers, severity, duration.
  - Reduce screen brightness and adjust workstation as needed; consider repeat eye test if eye strain suspected.
  - Return/seek review if headaches worsen, persist, or if new neurological symptoms (worsening vision, weakness) occur.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Offer prescription analgesia options (clinician discussed Naproxen; Paracetamol; Codeine) — prescription status not documented.
  - Advise correct ibuprofen dosing education noted (clinician stated ibuprofen can be taken up to two tablets three times daily) — patient previously taking approx. three tablets/day; dose/strength not documented.
  - Recommend headache diary and review in 1–2 weeks to consider prophylactic therapy if recurrent.
  - Advise urgent review or contact if vision changes, limb weakness, or systemic deterioration.

Secondary Problem: Work-related stress / concentration difficulties
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve concentration and reduce work impairment from headaches.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Address reversible contributors (pain control, screen adjustments) and monitor impact on work functioning.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Implement ergonomic/screen brightness adjustments; seek short-term workload modifications if needed.
  - Monitor stress and report ongoing impairment at follow-up.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Support with symptomatic management of headaches to improve concentration.
  - Reinforce workplace adjustments and consider referral if stress/anxiety persists (referral not documented).

Tertiary Problem: Photophobia / visual phenomena
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce light sensitivity and visual disturbance.
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Assess for ophthalmologic causes and manage photophobia symptomatically.
- Actions (Patient):
  - Reduce screen brightness; wear corrective lenses as usual; consider booking an eye test.
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Recommend repeat eye test given long interval since last test.
  - Advise monitoring of visual symptoms and urgent review if vision worsens.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Probable diagnosis (migraine-like headache) and family risk.
  - Analgesic options and appropriate dosing (ibuprofen dosing advised by clinician; alternatives discussed: naproxen, paracetamol, codeine).
  - Importance of headache diary and identifying triggers (hydration, stress, screen exposure).
  - When to seek urgent care: new/worsening vision problems, limb weakness, significant clinical deterioration.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing frequency of headaches, worsening pain, new visual disturbance, weakness in arms/legs, systemic unwellness.
- Coping Strategies:
  - Headache diary, hydration, screen brightness reduction, short-term workload adjustments, use of recommended analgesia.
